name: Ireland
summary: Misuse of Drugs Acts 1977–2016: possessing a controlled drug is a crime. Since 1 Sep 2026, Gardaí can refer first-time adult possession to the HSE instead of court. Selling other 'highs' is banned (2010 Act).
callingForHelp: No Good Samaritan law. Ambulance crews don't routinely involve Gardaí and medical confidentiality applies, but Gardaí may attend some scenes.
drugChecking: HSE runs free, anonymous 'back of house' drug checking at some festivals (Safer Nightlife, since 2022). No fixed-site service.

lsd.note: Schedule 1 controlled drug. First-time adult possession may be referred to the HSE (Health Referral Scheme, Sept 2026).

mushrooms.note: Any fungus containing psilocin is Schedule 1 (fresh mushrooms controlled since Jan 2006).

dmt.note: Schedule 1. Ayahuasca counts as a DMT preparation; a 2014 religious-exemption bid failed.

mescaline.note: Mescaline is Schedule 1. The cacti aren't listed by name, but mescaline prepared from them is controlled.

dox.note: Schedule 1: covered by the phenethylamine generic definition.

2c-x.note: Schedule 1: covered by the phenethylamine generic definition.

2c-t-x.note: Schedule 1: covered by the phenethylamine generic definition.

5-meo-xxt.note: Schedule 1: tryptamine generic plus ether clause covers 5-MeO-DMT and 5-MeO-MiPT.

cannabis.note: Schedule 1. Adult Caution Scheme and the HSE Health Referral Scheme (Sept 2026) can divert first offences. Medical Cannabis Access Programme exists.

ketamine.note: Schedule 3 controlled drug: possession without a prescription is an offence.

dxm.note: Not a controlled drug; sold in pharmacy cough medicines without prescription.

nitrous.note: Not controlled: possession isn't an offence, but selling it for inhalation is (2010 Act). EU ban on consumer sales expected from Feb 2027.

amphetamines.note: Amphetamine and methamphetamine are Schedule 2. ADHD medicines (lisdexamfetamine, methylphenidate) are legal with a prescription.

mdma.note: Schedule 1 controlled drug; possession is an offence.

cocaine.note: Schedule 2; possession is an offence (up to 7 years on indictment).

alcohol.note: Legal to buy from 18. Minimum unit pricing since January 2022.

ghb/gbl.note: GHB is Schedule 2. GBL and 1,4-BD are controlled; possession is lawful only if not for human ingestion.

opioids.note: Heroin and opioids like morphine, oxycodone and fentanyl are Schedule 2; legal only with a prescription. Low-dose codeine is pharmacy-only.

tramadol.note: Prescription-only, but not listed in the 2017 Misuse of Drugs Regulations: possession isn't a drugs offence; supply without prescription is.

benzodiazepines.note: Schedule 4 Part 1: possession without a prescription has been an offence since May 2017 (also z-drugs).

maois.note: Medical MAOIs are prescription-only, not controlled. Harmala/Syrian rue aren't scheduled (selling as a high is banned). Ayahuasca is illegal (DMT).

ssris.note: Prescription-only but not controlled: possession isn't an offence; supply without a prescription is.
